cim: University of Indianapolis receives $8.5 million grant to establish new Center for Artificial Intelligence for Human Performance, help prepare students for future
cim_eredeti: University of Indianapolis receives $8.5 million grant to establish new Center for Artificial Intelligence for Human Performance, help prepare students for future
szoveg_eredeti:
The University of Indianapolis has been awarded an $8.5 million grant from Lilly Endowment Inc. to create a new Center for Artificial Intelligence for Human Performance and significantly expand the use of AI on campus. The grant is part of Lilly Endowment’s Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education (AIHE) initiative, which is designed to help Indiana colleges and universities address the challenges and opportunities of AI. UIndy’s approach focuses on preparing students for a rapidly evolving workforce while helping Indiana businesses and nonprofits adapt to the emerging technology.

The three-year initiative is a major investment in the University’s academic programs, faculty development and infrastructure. In addition to the creation of the Center for AI, plans call for creating or revising up to 330 courses to incorporate AI into the curriculum, developing nine AI-focused micro-credentials and giving new opportunities for students to get hands-on experience through industry-sponsored projects.

“Artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing the way we live and work at breathtaking speeds. Higher education has a responsibility to prepare students not just to use these new tools, but to think critically about how and why they are used,” said University of Indianapolis President Tanuja Singh. “This investment helps us build on our strengths as an institution that emphasizes experiential learning and student-centered education, while also expanding our Education for Service motto to help businesses and organizations navigate these changes. We must ensure that technology serves people, not the other way around.”

“The rapid rise and growing ubiquity of AI may be one of the most significant challenges higher education institutions have ever faced,” said Ted Maple, the Endowment’s vice president for education. “Faculty and staff are concerned about the potential for AI to, among other things, impede original and independent thinking and threaten social connections. Yet at the same time, colleges and universities have recognized that AI may also present unprecedented opportunities for their institutions to enhance teaching and learning, student services, research capabilities and more. We are pleased to be able to help higher education institutions in Indiana find the best ways they can respond to these challenges and opportunities.”

The AIHE grant will also support significant investments in the University’s technology infrastructure, including AI-powered tools to improve academic advising, student support services, transfer credit evaluations and data security. In addition, faculty will receive training and resources to incorporate AI into their courses, with an emphasis on critical thinking and ethical decision making to prepare students to use the technology responsibly in their chosen career field.

The Center for Artificial Intelligence for Human Performance will be housed in a renovated area in UIndy’s Krannert Memorial Library. One strategic pillar of the Center will be thought leadership, serving as a hub for both campus and community conversations about how AI intersects with human performance. The other strategic pillar will focus on applied learning and consulting by providing customized services to nonprofits and small businesses that often lack the resources or expertise to adopt AI effectively on their own.

“The Center for Artificial Intelligence for Human Performance is particularly exciting because it pairs the expertise of our faculty and the creative energy and problem-solving abilities of our students to address the real-world challenges facing Hoosier businesses and organizations,” said UIndy Provost Chris Plouff. “Our students will benefit greatly from the hands-on experience they gain by applying what they learn in the classroom. Our entire state will benefit from new ideas and practical solutions. It’s the kind of community partnership that showcases UIndy’s commitment to its mission of service for impact.”

The initiative is expected to begin in January and builds on the University of Indianapolis’s ongoing work in artificial intelligence. UIndy hosted its inaugural AI Summit in April to bring together business leaders, educators, tech experts and policymakers to explore the opportunities and challenges of AI. The summit will return in the fall of 2027.

Lilly Endowment’s initiative, Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education is designed to support colleges and universities in Indiana as they develop and implement approaches for using artificial intelligence. The grants will help ensure that their students, faculty and staff are well-equipped to learn, work and live in a world increasingly influenced by AI. The University of Indianapolis is one of 35 colleges and universities in Indiana receiving funding through the initiative.

For more information or to arrange an interview, please contact UIndy’s Director of Public & Media Relations Dan Klein.
